Hi! Has anyone gotten the tex blocks working with verso-blueprint? I tried taking the project-template and adding the following tex block in Addition.lean:

```tex
\begin{align}
  1 & 2 & 3
\end{align}
```

however the changes don't appear in the output after running lake exe blueprint-gen --verbose --output _out. The entire TeX-block is simply ignored.

I have read the manual but didn't find any hints. The manual just says Blueprint nodes can also store raw general-TeX source through `tex` code blocks, and doesn't mention if some flag or option needs to be enabled for the tex to end up in the HTML.

We are trying to get started with using verso-blueprint in formalization summer projects at Aalto University. It might be that we are just misunderstanding the purpose of these TeX-blocks -- perhaps they only appear when emitting TeX? Any help would be appreciated!

It is $$`foo` for normal equation blocks, I don't know whether it is possible to make align work.
Edit: $$`\begin{aligned}foo &= 0\\bar &= 1\end{aligned}` works

Hi @Niklas Halonen , sorry for the poor documentation.

As of today TeX blocks are used to validate porting from TeX to Verso and indeed they are not displayed.

I'll improve the documentation.

What's your use case for using TeX? Would you like to be able to write content using TeX?

Thaks for the explanation @Emilio Jesús Gallego Arias ! Our use case is to migrate an old leanblueprint to verso-blueprint. We initially hoped that it would be possible to copy TeX code blocks (and not just the math mode) straight over using the ```tex blocks. Instead it appears that we need to do more manual rewriting (partially due to KaTeX limitations). I guess there is also no way to have a latex processor running as part of a verso-blueprint HTML generation?

We often do this in a semi-automated way using https://github.com/ejgallego/leanblueprint-to-verso (requires to use an agent for translation, but we could explore having an agent-free version)

I'd be happy to run the tool on your blueprint if it's public.

We could explore running a latex processor, in a best-effort basis if that would be useful.

The main use for tex blocks right now is a translation review interface, which I plan to land ASAP, see it for example in action here https://x80.org/flt-translation-review/

Thanks for the offer, but we don't use AI (and also don't accept AI contributions)... I'll take a look at leanblueprint-to-verso to see if it contains any scripts that could help.

The TeX review does look like a helpful feature to verify the AI-based workflow.

I think it could also help to verify a "hacky regex-based translation script" review, if you have a script that can generate some initial Verso version of the content in a deterministic way. The tool could draw your attention to the places where the content fell outside what the script was good at.

@𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒 also suggested a pandoc backend from TeX to Verso, we could try to use it.

@Niklas Halonen I'm much afraid that leanblueprint-to-verso is very tailored to an LLM-based workflow, so it won't be useful in that case. Using LLMs for translation makes sense, as in fact the transformer architecture was develop precisely for this use case.
